From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@peregrinelabs.com, csm@peregrinelabs.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: QBR slate recalibration: product & eng readiness, timelines, and contingency asks

Team —

QBR is next Wednesday (9/8). I took an early pass at the slate and we need to recalibrate the product/eng section based on current delivery signals. High-level objectives for this thread:

- Surface the specific launch timelines that have shifted and why.
- Agree on go/no-go triggers we can present at the QBR (no fuzzy language).
- Confirm the minimal canary scope + rollback plan to share with Peregrine Ops.

Attached: qbr_slatedelta.xlsx (draft slide with suggested changes), eng_risk_log.pdf (current risk register). Also added a placeholder MAP for Peregrine (mutual-action-plan.docx).

Please reply with one-line readiness level (Green/Yellow/Red), the single highest-risk dependency, and the preferred canary date by EOD today. I want an updated consolidated slide before EOD tomorrow so I can brief the execs on Thursday morning.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Dir, Customer Strategy — Redwood Inference

---

Attachments: qbr_slatedelta.xlsx (xlsx, 128KB), eng_risk_log.pdf (pdf, 550KB), mutual-action-plan.docx (docx, 220KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR slate recalibration: product & eng readiness, timelines, and contingency asks

Naomi —

Readiness: Yellow.

Top-line engineering update (summary):
- Core inference path: on track for model freeze 9/3, but two infra items remain (GPU image validation + CI perf regression) that could add 3–5 business days if regressions surface.
- Canary scope: recommend shrinking to 10% traffic and single-region (us-west-2) to reduce blast radius; that buys time for the remaining infra validation.
- Highest-risk dependency: third-party kernel backport (vendor team has one remaining commit outstanding). If that commit delays >48h we'll miss the 9/10 canary target.

Preferred canary date (proposal): 2027-09-10 (assuming backport lands by 9/2). If backport slips, fallback canary on 2027-09-15 with reduced scope.

Action items I can deliver by EOD: updated timeline slide (will push to the drive link), concise rollback plan for canary, and a short list of mitigations for the backport risk (including vendor escalation notes).

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: QBR slate recalibration: product & eng readiness, timelines, and contingency asks

Naomi/Karthik —

Readiness: Yellow -> leaning Red for customer messaging risk. From the customer success side, Peregrine has been expecting an early-September rollout; they will read any slip as a de-prioritization unless we give them a tight MAP with concrete milestones and an explicit rollback SLA.

Suggested mitigations:
- Share a 3-point MAP (I attached mutual-action-plan.docx) with dates for: vendor backport acceptance, internal perf signoff, and canary start. Each point should have an owner and a 24–48h contingency step we can trigger.
- Customer comms: propose a short note acknowledging the shift and committing to the reduced-scope canary + weekly checkpoint cadence. Lina, can you draft?
- If we move the canary to 9/15, request a temporary credit or extended support window as a gesture — flagging this for finance/sales.

Attaching mutual-action-plan.docx here for versioning. I also exported a brief risk summary into eng_risk_log.pdf (see page 2 for impact table).

Monica
Sr Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR slate recalibration: product & eng readiness, timelines, and contingency asks

Thanks all —

Readiness: Yellow (operationally manageable, reputation risk if communications are poor). Decisions for execs:

1) Canary commitment: pick one date only to present at QBR (either 9/10 with vendor backport confirmation or 9/15 as conservative). Present both options but be explicit on the trigger that moves us from optimistic -> conservative.
2) Go/no-go criteria: vendor backport accepted AND internal perf gate passed AND canary rollback tested in staging within 24h. No partial language.
3) Customer ask: offer Peregrine the weekly checkpoint and consider a one-time credit if we move to 9/15. Team, give me the credit estimate and message language by EOD tomorrow.

Naomi, Karthik: get the consolidated slide with the single-line readiness, the top dependency, and the chosen canary date into the drive. Exec briefing Thursday morning — I need a single slide that is defensible.

Vivek
VP Product & Strategy

Thanks Naomi / team —

Appreciate the transparency. Peregrine can accept a reduced-scope canary and the weekly checkpoint cadence. Two asks from our side before we confirm the new date:

1) Can you share the rollback SLA in writing (what triggers rollback, expected RTO for failing canary paths)?
2) If we move to 9/15, can Redwood commit to a temporary expanded support window for the first 72h post-canary?

If you can put both items in the MAP and confirm the owner, we can sign off internally and be ready for the canary window.

Samir Desai
Head of Platform Operations — Peregrine Labs
